newsitem.title: USA: Fidelity Investments to layoff about 1 pct - WSJ.
newsitem.headline: Fidelity Investments to layoff about 1 pct - WSJ.

text.p: Fidelity Investments is about to usher in a new era of austerity with plans to lay off between 280 and 300 employees, the Wall Street Journal said.
In Wednesday's electronic edition, the Journal said the layoffs represent a little more than 1 percent of the company's 24,000 employees.
The Journal, quoting unidentified company insiders, said Fidelity is also cutting advertising spending slightly, holding technology spending steady and reviewing costs across the board.
David Weinstein, senior vice president of administration, said the brokerage and mutual fund firm is in a midyear "course correction" on expenditures.

"We've had a remarkable spurt of growth," Weinstein said. "For any company that has grown so rapidly, the real challenge is to take a look at the players we have on the team and make sure we're using them well."
Fidelity Chief Operating Officer James Curvey added: "I'm looking at expenses across the board. Everybody is looking at expenses."
